correctness.rationale: For each cycle, dividing configuration weights by the all-open product gives independent closed-edge activities rho_e=w_e^-1 (forest) or q/w_e (FK), with empty-support bonus kappa=0 or q. For two vertex-pair arc partitions, the numerator of support-containment covariance equals SU-RC+kappa(U+S-R-C), with x,y,z,w four nonnegative cell activities. I independently expanded the displayed polynomial identities with SymPy and obtained zero differences and nonnegative coefficients. Cyclomatic identity k(F)=|V|-|F|+c(F) on a cactus exactly separates bridge/cycle block factors, so the two global pair events decompose as products of local connectivity requirements along unique block-cut routes. Independent blocks and local covariance inequality imply global covariance >=0 for all q>0 (including 0<q<1), forest law and arbitrary positive weights. Bridge-only, empty route and repeated vertices are harmless. This is a structural proof, not finite-case extrapolation.
